title: Inverse function theorem with a C¹ inverse on an open neighbourhood
statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, h : ℝ^d → ℝ^d, V ⊆ ℝ^d open and v₀ ∈ V. Suppose h is C¹ on V and its Fréchet derivative at v₀ is the identity, Dh(v₀) = id_{ℝ^d}. Then there are open sets V₀, O ⊆ ℝ^d and a map k : ℝ^d → ℝ^d such that V₀ ⊆ V, v₀ ∈ V₀, h(V₀) ⊆ O, k(O) ⊆ V₀, k(h(v)) = v for all v ∈ V₀, h(k(u)) = u for all u ∈ O, k is C¹ on O, and the Fréchet derivative of k at h(v₀) is the identity.
lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (h : Euclid d → Euclid d) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (v₀ : Euclid d), IsOpen V → v₀ ∈ V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h V → fderiv ℝ h v₀ = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid d) → ∃ (V₀ O : Set (Euclid d)) (k : Euclid d → Euclid d), IsOpen V₀ ∧ IsOpen O ∧ V₀ ⊆ V ∧ v₀ ∈ V₀ ∧ MapsTo h V₀ O ∧ MapsTo k O V₀ ∧ (∀ v ∈ V₀, k (h v) = v) ∧ (∀ u ∈ O, h (k u) = u) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 k O ∧ fderiv ℝ k (h v₀) = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid d)
